APX-000054.transcript:
Customer (Michael Stewart): My bill jumped and I don't understand why. Did something change with my rate?
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Hi Michael Stewart, Kagiso Radebe here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Michael Stewart): I've been on the same rate for years, why is this changing now?
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Happy to explain it. Let me pull up your usage first.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (Michael Stewart): Yes, same address as always, and the account's under my name.
Customer (Michael Stewart): Is this the Phase 2 thing the AUC approved, or did I do something wrong on my account?
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Did you get the letter by mail or by email?
Customer (Michael Stewart): By mail, a couple of weeks ago.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Do you have any irrigation or shop meters on the same account?
Customer (Michael Stewart): No, just the house.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Let me take a look. I've pulled up the account, confirmed the Rate 1/Rate 2 threshold under the August 1 Phase 2 restructuring, and walked through what changed on this specific account.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Since August 1, Rate 1 covers accounts using under 4,000 GJ a year and Rate 2 covers larger users. The AUC approved it as Phase 2 of the rate restructuring.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Your usage puts you right at the edge of the new Rate 2 threshold, so this bill reflects the higher rate class — I don't have authority to move you back to Rate 1 manually, that's set by your metered usage under the AUC-approved structure.
Customer (Michael Stewart): Can't you just put me back on Rate 1?
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Not manually. The class follows your metered usage under the approved structure.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): To recap: your usage puts you in Rate 2 for now, the class is reviewed against annual usage, and the details are in your email.
Customer (Michael Stewart): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
